title: Taking Photos in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Outdoors, you are covered.** Section 59 of the German copyright act lets you photograph and publish works permanently on public paths, roads and open spaces. For buildings, that covers the façade. Every stop on my walking tour sits in this category.

**The Humboldt Forum runs four different rules in one building.** Tripods and flash are allowed in the outdoor courtyards, private photos are fine on the roof terrace and the upper museum floors, and two first-floor exhibitions ban photography completely.
**BERLIN GLOBAL and the Humboldt Lab are camera-off.** Both prohibit all photographic and film recordings, private and commercial alike. BERLIN GLOBAL marks the motifs with pictograms.
**On Museum Island the bag is the checkpoint, not the camera.** The state museums require camera cases, tripods, umbrellas and any bag larger than 30 x 20 x 10 cm to go to the cloakroom or a locker.
**Selfie sticks are banned in the state museums,** along with laser pointers. Only pencils may be used in the exhibition rooms.
**Any single exhibition can be declared camera-free.** The museum management board holds that right, so the sign at that door beats anything you read in advance.
**The TV Tower allows private photos but no tripods and no drones.** Backpacks must fit inside 45 x 35 x 20 cm, security is airport-style, and there are no lockers at all.

**The Holocaust Memorial's Information Centre turns bags away.** Suitcases and small bags may not enter, lockers are at Friedrichstraße and Potsdamer Platz, and the foundation asks for appropriate behaviour inside.

**Drones over central Berlin are effectively out.** Government seats, embassies, police property, federal trunk roads, railway installations and federal waterways all carry 100 metre restrictions, and the Berliner Spree is a federal waterway.

**Publishing a photo of a stranger is the regulated act, not taking it.** German law needs consent to publish a portrait, with an exception for people who appear only as an incidental part of a wider scene.
